subject: Issues with geom_density: closed curve problems

messages.author: 3a775dfa0a96bf95
messages.subject: Issues with geom_density: closed curve problems
parts:
geom_density plots the density curve but also a horizontal line (y=0);
it also always forces the curve to go through (x=0,y=0), all
apparently to form a closed curve (why?). This is a fairly minor
annoyance:

ggplot(data.frame(a=rexp(1000))) + geom_density(aes(x=a))

But if we put the density on a logarithmic scale, the closing line is
at the top of the graph and looks terrible:

ggplot(data.frame(a=rexp(1000))) + geom_density(aes(x=a)) + scale_y_log10()

Especially ugly when the curve goes above the axis:

ggplot(data.frame(a=c(rep(1,1000),rexp(1000)))) +
geom_density(aes(x=a)) + scale_y_log10()

Also, using scale limits results in rather poor results:

set.seed(1); dd <- data.frame(a=c(rep(1,10000),rexp(1000)))
ggplot(dd) + geom_density(aes(x=a)) + scale_y_log10(limits=c(1e-3,1))

The slicing-off at the top and bottom isn't clean (the line continues
where it should have disappeared, and the line isn't horizontal) and
the "return" line around to the right is a function of where exactly
the distribution was cut off, which is awful.

Somewhat better is to use coord_ to limit the graph:

ggplot(dd) + geom_density(aes(x=a)) +
scale_y_log10(breaks=10^seq(-2,1,by=.5)) +
coord_cartesian(ylim=c(-2,1))

but this still leaves the "return" line on the left, middle, and
right. (as well as being inconvenient since the coord limits are in
log space, not in data space; and because the scale breaks aren't
calculated automatically for this zoom level).

-s

geom_density <- function(...) stat_density(..., geom = "line",
position = "identity")
